pressure_cooker.note: Simmer covered about 20 min longer until dal or vegetables are soft; top up water as needed.

kadai.note: Any heavy-bottomed pot works for deep-frying and simmering.
Fine for shallow-frying and sauteing; less depth for deep-frying.

tawa.note: A flat dosa griddle works for rotis and phulkas.
A flat non-stick pan stands in for a griddle; watch for hot spots.

dosa_tawa.note: A regular flat griddle works; season well so batter does not stick.
Use a wide flat non-stick pan; spread batter thinner.

mixer_grinder.note: Works for wet pastes and chutneys; add a little water to help it turn.
Good for coarse pastes and chopping; less smooth for fine spice powders.
Pound small quantities of spices or ginger-garlic by hand.

wet_grinder.note: Grind idli/dosa batter in small batches; pulse and rest to avoid overheating.
Grind in small batches with cold water; batter is slightly less fluffy.

blender.note: Handles the same wet grinding jobs.
For thicker mixes; add liquid for smooth blends.

food_processor.note: Use the dry/chutney jar for chopping and coarse pastes.
Chop by hand when the quantity is small.

idli_steamer.note: Steam without the weight/whistle so pressure does not build.
Place the idli stand on a trivet over a little water and cover to steam.

idli_stand.note: Steam batter in small greased steel bowls or cups instead of moulds.

appam_pan.note: Use a small deep kadai; swirl batter up the sides for the lacy edge.

paniyaram_pan.note: Shallow-fry spoonfuls of batter in a kadai; you lose the round shape.

mortar_pestle.note: Pulse briefly for a coarse crush; do not over-grind to a paste.
Pulse in short bursts for small quantities.

rolling_pin.note: Use the smooth side of a cylindrical tumbler or bottle to roll dough.

rolling_board.note: A clean flat board or the counter dusted with flour works fine.

grater.note: Finely chop or julienne by hand instead of grating.
Use the grating/shredding disc if available.

whisk.note: Blend or froth curd, batter or decoction quickly.
Beat with a fork against the side of the bowl for small quantities.

oven.note: Dry-roast or bake in a covered heavy kadai over low heat with a little salt at the base.
For reheating and quick bakes; will not brown or crisp like an oven.

colander.note: Drain smaller quantities through a fine sieve.

strainer.note: For coarse straining; fine particles may pass through.

slotted_spoon.note: Tilt to drain oil against the pan side; slower but works.
Lift fried items and let excess oil drip off.

saucepan.note: Any small heavy pot works for boiling milk or making decoction.
Fine for heating liquids in small batches.

tongs.note: Flip rotis or fried items with a flat turner instead.
